newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Nitroil plans to stay on Budapest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Nitroil plans to stay on Budapest bourse.

text.p: A recent meeting of Hungarian chemical engineering firm Nitroil Rt shareholders decided not to delist the firm from the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE), Nitroil managing director Tamas Drozda told Reuters.

"The main shareholder asked for the opinion of the board of directors and then decided not delist the company," he said. "It was the second time that the shareholder had asked and I don't think he will do it again."
Drozda said, Nitroil's main shareholder was John M.T. King with a 49.97 percent stake, while his wife, Margaret King owned 20.45 percent of the shares.

Drozda said delisting made no sense as according to the securities law, companies which have registered capital of over 200 million forints must be listed on the BSE by the end of 1998 and while Nitroil was a larger firm than that.
Drozda said the shareholders' meeting also voted against the dematerialization of Nitroil's shares.
"The law allows dematerialization, but the conditions for that at (the central clearing house) KELER and brokerage companies are not ensured," he said.
The company's shares are among the most illiquid stocks traded on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE).
Nitroil closed at 21,150 forints on the BSE on February 25, the last day it was traded.
